prompt: Recreate, from scratch, the hero animation on OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra landing page as a single self-contained HTML page with a canvas animation. It is a SPIRAL GALAXY that reads as the numeral 6, sitting between the words GPT and Astra on a near-black field. A bright bloomed core, logarithmic spiral arms winding outward, several hundred star particles of varying size, mostly white and pale blue with scattered warm amber accents, a few bright stars carrying 4-point diffraction spikes. The whole spiral turns slowly, and it turns DIFFERENTIALLY: the core sweeps faster than the rim, so the arms wind up over time. Write your own implementation; do not copy any existing code.
definition_of_done: final_output_file: galaxy.html, one self-contained HTML page. All cases in test_acceptance.py pass via `python -I -m unittest discover -s . -v` with exit code 0. The page starts with <!doctype html>, contains a <canvas>, drives animation with requestAnimationFrame, and makes ZERO external requests: no http(s) src or href, no @import, no url(//...), no fetch, no XMLHttpRequest. Everything inline. It must contain <script id="galaxy-model" type="module"> exporting a PURE function `points(t)` that returns the particle array for time t in seconds. That script is executed on its own in node by the gate, so it must not mention canvas, document, window or getContext - pure math only. The renderer is separate and calls it. Measured, not asserted: points(t) returns 400-20000 particles; every particle has finite numeric x, y and a positive r; more particles fall inside 25% of the max radius than beyond 75% of it (dense core); over 12 seconds most particles change angle; mean angular sweep for particles at 5-30% radius exceeds that at 60-100% radius by at least 15% (differential rotation); and binning particle angles into 36 buckets, the busiest bucket exceeds 1.6x the mean (spiral arms, not an even disc). If the contract cannot be satisfied, return status='failure' with the precise reason rather than a page that games the tests.
contract:
Return ONE complete HTML document in the `code` field, from <!doctype html> to </html>. Structure it as model plus renderer:
1. <script id="galaxy-model" type="module"> containing ONLY pure math and `export function points(t) { ... }`. It returns an array of objects each with numeric x, y (centred on 0,0) and r (radius in px), and may add colour or brightness fields. No canvas, document, window or getContext anywhere in this block - the gate runs it standalone in node and greps for those words.
2. A separate <script> that owns the <canvas>, sizes it to the viewport, and on each requestAnimationFrame calls points(elapsedSeconds) and draws them.
Model requirements: a logarithmic spiral with 2 or 3 arms; particle density falling off with radius so the core is dense; per-particle angular velocity decreasing with radius (differential rotation) so arms wind; deterministic for a given t, since the gate calls points(0) and points(12) and compares them.
Render requirements: near-black background, additive or lighter compositing for glow, a bloomed core, size and alpha varying per particle, a white/pale-blue majority with warm amber accents, and a handful of bright stars with 4-point spikes. Show the words GPT and Astra either side of the galaxy. Everything inline: no external fonts, images, scripts or network calls of any kind.
